title: API-First Quickstarts & Pricing Phrasing Lab
content:
Purpose
This is a working lab for short, testable messaging blocks and pricing microcopy aimed at early developer activation for the Hosted API. Goal is to produce 4–6 distinct quickstart angles and 6 concise pricing/FAQ phrasings we can A/B test across signup, docs, and pricing pages.

Audience / Personas
- Indie app founders & startup engineers: want speed-to-prototype, low friction, clear cost signals.
- Platform/infra engineers at SMBs: care about latency predictability and quotas.
- Experimentation teams at mid-market: want guardrails (rate limits, rollbacks) and usage forecasting.

Core developer-first value props (headline candidates)
1) "Build in minutes, scale with predictable economics" — emphasise quickstart + unit-cost signals.
2) "Same API from prototype to production" — highlight parity with Dedicated/Private.
3) "Latency you can budget for, cost you can control" — tie to Optimize suggestions (batching, caching).
4) "Start free, pay for what you use (per-token transparency)" — simple pricing heuristic.

Quickstart angle sketches (short copy + primary CTA)
A. Minimal friction ("Hello World in 3 requests")
- Short copy: "No signup hooks, no infra. API key in 30s, generate text in 3 requests."
- CTA: "Get API key — try the example"
- Hook: embed a runnable curl + response in the landing page.

B. Cost-aware prototype ("Prototype with cost estimates")
- Short copy: "Build a prototype and see estimated token costs as you iterate."
- CTA: "Run estimator on your prompt"
- Hook: inline cost estimator in quickstart that shows expected per-turn cost for sample prompts.

C. Latency-first QA ("99th percentile latency in your region")
- Short copy: "Test your prompt in your region. We surface p50/p95/p99 so you know what to expect."
- CTA: "Check latency for my prompt"
- Hook: small latency widget in docs that runs a short synthetic request to the hosted endpoint (sandbox).

D. Tooling-driven onboarding ("SDKs, snippets, and infra patterns")
- Short copy: "Ship faster with official SDKs and templates for chat, embeddings, and streaming."
- CTA: "Open starter repo"
- Hook: deep-linked GitHub template with one-click deploy instructions.

Pricing microcopy options (concise phrase + elaboration)
1) "Pay per token, zero surprises" — "Tokens billed as input + output; daily usage dashboard and cost alerts."
2) "Free trial credits + transparent unit pricing" — "$X in credits, real-time estimator, upgrade to per-token billing anytime."
3) "Committed plans for steady throughput" — "Reserved capacity reduces per-token cost and guarantees throughput; ideal for production workloads."
4) "Predictable SLO tiers" — "Choose a latency SLA (standard/priority) and opt into fallback routing to keep apps online during capacity events."
5) "Developer-friendly volume discounts" — "Auto-applied discounts as monthly token usage crosses thresholds (no complex contract required)."
6) "Per-route cost controls" — "Set per-route caps or per-token max to avoid runaway bills during experiments."

Pricing examples (micro math for copy)
- Maker example: "Prototype chat: 10k inference tokens/day ~ $2/day at $0.0002/token."
- SMB production: "200k tokens/day with reserved plan -> effective $0.00012/token (committed discount)."

Competitive quick notes (what to call out vs others)
- Versus large API-first vendors: emphasize latency transparency, configurable SLOs, and unit-cost breakdowns at token level.
- Versus infra-only vendors/self-hosted runtimes: highlight unified onramp (no infra), curated models, and a path to Dedicated/Private.
- Versus low-cost providers: call out production features — auditing, rollouts, canarying, and predictable throughput.

Common objections + suggested counters
- Objection: "Hosted is easy now but expensive at scale."
  Counter: "We provide Optimize recommendations, batching/caching, and committed plans to lower unit cost — plus transparent dashboards so you can track ops impact."
- Objection: "Model lock-in concern."
  Counter: "We support model pinning, variant rollouts, and migration tooling; same API across hosted/Dedicated/Private for portability."
- Objection: "Security/compliance for regulated data."
  Counter: "Private deployments and Dedicated capacity options with audit logs and KMS integration; list page for compliance features."

Microcopy snippets to lift into UI (short, testable)
- Signup modal (short): "Create an API key — start building in 30s. Free credits included."
- Inline quickstart header: "Hello world: run a chat request, view tokens, and estimate cost."
- Pricing CTA: "Estimate your monthly cost" (opens cost-estimator)
- Billing alert copy: "Alert: route 'experiment-foo' hit 75% of its daily cap."

Experiments and measurement plan (quick)
- Variants: Test three headline plus CTA combos across landing hero, quickstart docs, and pricing page.
- Metrics: sign-ups with API key created, first-3-requests completion, billing upgrade rate, time-to-first-successful-response, churn at 30 days.
- Sample A/B: Hero headline A (speed) vs B (cost transparency) with identical CTAs; measure conversion to API-key creation.

Next steps (actionable)
1) Pick 3 hero headline candidates and 2 quickstart flows to implement as interactive widgets by 2025-10-10.
2) Wire cost-estimator snippet into docs sandbox (ownership: DevEx, PR GIT-PR-8421).
3) Prepare two pricing microcopy variants for pricing page rollout experiment (owner: Omar).
4) Sync with Product (Priya) on telemetry events required for the measurement plan.

Notes / open questions
- Need legal sign-off on free credit amount and terms (contacts: Finance & Legal).
- Verify which regions can run the sandbox latency widget without violating data residency policies.
- Decide if per-route caps require backend changes or can be implemented as a soft quota in the console.

Quick links and references
- Benchmark doc: https://confluence.redwood/example-hosted-api-benchmarks (linked above)
- DevEx starter repo: GIT-PR-8421
- GTM ticket: JIRA-GTM-309

Status: WORKING DRAFT — intended for quick iteration and copy experiments.
